candidates.title: DDPT: Enhancing complex reasoning in large language models via distillation and dynamic prompt tuning
candidates.reason: Relevant to LLM inference: beyond parameter-efficient prompt tuning during adaptation, DDPT changes test-time execution by routing each query to a specialized soft prompt using similarity and using a soft-prompt verifier with majority voting to filter generated reasoning paths. The paper reports an average accuracy gain of 8.39% over 100-token prompt tuning at comparable parameter count and performance above LoRA with fewer parameters; it does not establish inference latency or throughput gains, so acceptance is for inference reasoning behavior rather than serving-speed improvement.
candidates.library_body_check: Primary ScienceDirect article text for Neurocomputing 698 (2026), article 134297, was checked beyond its abstract: Introduction describes soft-prompt underfitting and the cost/ineffectiveness of simply lengthening prompts; the method description specifies distillation from few-shot hard-prompt demonstrations into multiple shorter specialized soft prompts, similarity-based pre-inference routing, and post-inference soft-prompt verification with majority voting; Implementation details names LLaMA-2-13B, LLaMA-3-8B, Mistral-v0.2-7B, and Qwen-2.5-7B; reported result is +8.39% average accuracy versus a 100-token PT baseline at comparable trainable parameters and outperforming LoRA with fewer parameters. The paper's Dependency on data section states effectiveness may degrade when LLM-generated training data is poor, including low baseline accuracy or weak generalization in a 1-shot setting. ScienceDirect indexed the article body and these sections, while direct page open returned 403; no latency/throughput result was verified. The local repository clone is at 25364b003e69f031153a4f0b22c030c30034ea86 rather than the brief's pinned 8aa06282382aa6c050ad18fcc6bdcbd23337e321; therefore no canonical duplicate/nonexistence claim is made here and current-main precheck remains necessary.
